records.title: Molecular Signatures of HIV-Induced Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration in Human Cerebral Organoids: Identification of Therapeutic Targets for NeuroHIV.
records.abstract: HIV-associated neurological complications remain a major concern in people living with HIV (PWH), even under effective viral suppression with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), underscoring unresolved mechanisms driving HIV-related neurodegeneration. To address this gap, we used HIV-1-infected human cerebral organoids (hCOs) containing microglia as a physiologically relevant three-dimensional model of the central nervous system (CNS) and validated key findings in the brain region of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infected, cART-treated rhesus macaque model. Integrated single-nucleus RNA sequencing with ATAC-seq (multi-omics), identifies cell-type-specific alterations in dual innate immune-driven inflammatory signaling pathways across neural and glial populations in hCOs. Microglia were preferentially infected and activated, initiating IL-17A-mediated cascades involving IFN-γ/STAT1, CEBPB, and NF-κB signaling. These pathways converged with cGAS-STING and Notch-NEURL1 signaling, both associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction. cART suppressed viral replication, reduced IL-17A-mediated neuroinflammation, improved mitochondrial function, and restored synaptic gene expression. Collectively, these findings identify dysregulation of IL-17A, STAT1, CEBPB, and cGAS-STING signaling as key molecular drivers of HIV-associated neuroinflammation. They also establish a potential mechanistic link between IL-17A signaling and microglial remodeling, providing a translational framework for the development of CNS-targeted therapies in PWH.

records.title: 2-Hydroxyisobutyrylation of SRSF9 Regulates CD44 Alternative Splicing to Promote Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastasis.
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major cause of cancer mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that remodel metastatic RNA-splicing programs are poorly defined. Here, integrated quantitative proteomics and lysine 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation (Khib) proteomics of patient-matched normal mucosa, primary CRCs, and liver metastases revealed a progressive increase in global Khib, with enrichment on RNA-splicing proteins. Serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 9 (SRSF9) emerged as a Khib-modified splicing factor whose expression and K155 Khib levels increased from normal tissue to primary tumors and liver metastases. Gain and loss of function studies in CRC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, subcutaneous xenografts, and splenic injection liver metastasis models showed that SRSF9 promotes proliferation, invasion, tumor growth, and liver colonization. Mechanistically, K155 Khib stabilized SRSF9 protein; the K155R mutation accelerated degradation and abolished SRSF9-driven malignant phenotypes. KAT7 and SIRT6 act as regulators of Khib modification, which positively and negatively modulate the K155 Khib modification of SRSF9, respectively. SRSF9 bound CD44 pre-mRNA through its RRM1 domain and promoted alternative splicing toward the oncogenic CD44V8-10 isoform, which was elevated in patient tumors and metastases and rescued the impaired proliferation and metastatic capacity caused by SRSF9 loss. Finally, a CD44V8-10-targeting antisense oligonucleotide suppressed CRC growth and liver metastasis in preclinical models. These findings define a KAT7/SIRT6-regulated Khib-SRSF9-CD44V8-10 axis that couples metabolic acylation to metastatic splicing and nominate CD44V8-10 as a therapeutic vulnerability in CRC liver metastasis.

records.title: Nebulization-stable lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery in advanced in vitro respiratory models.
records.abstract: Pulmonary delivery of messenger RNA (mRNA) offers a promising strategy for local vaccination and treating respiratory diseases, but aerosolization stress and airway barriers remain major obstacles. Here, we developed PEG-free lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles (mucLPs) composed of a solid polylactic acid (PLA) core and an engineered lipid corona. Nine formulations were screened by varying lipid composition and were evaluated for physicochemical properties, mRNA association, cytocompatibility, stability during vibrating-mesh nebulization, and transfection. The lead formulation, mucLP3, combined high mRNA association with a negative post-loading surface charge and preserved its size distribution and reporter activity after nebulization. By contrast, the SM-102-based reference LNP tested under the same conditions showed aggregation and reduced reporter expression after nebulization. Non-nebulized mucLP3 also supported mRNA expression in airway epithelial cell lines, mouse lung organoids, and primary human airway epithelial cultures maintained at an air-liquid interface. These data establish a proof of concept for a PEG-free lipid-polymer hybrid architecture that tolerates the tested nebulization procedure and remains functional in respiratory models of increasing complexity. Direct mucus-transport measurements, aerosol-deposition studies, and in vivo efficacy studies will be required to establish pulmonary delivery performance.

records.title: Efficient Generation of Definitive-like Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cells from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells through Optimized Lateral Plate Mesoderm Induction and a Supportive Endothelial-Stromal Microenvironment.
records.abstract: The generation of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) with definitive features from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) requires coordinated lineage specification together with a supportive hematopoietic microenvironment. Although 3D and aggregate-based systems can recapitulate endothelial and stromal niche features, their self-organizing architecture can introduce structural heterogeneity and batch-to-batch variability, complicating experimental standardization and process control. Here, we developed a chemically defined, feeder-free, lateral plate mesoderm (LPM)-directed 2D multicellular system that combines controlled hematopoietic specification with the spontaneous formation of an endothelial-stromal microenvironment. Through sequential differentiation from LPM to hemogenic endothelium, this system generated CD34+CD43+CD45+ HSPCs at frequencies of up to 86% across three hPSC lines within 10 days. Notably, an endothelial-stromal microenvironment formed spontaneously without aggregate formation, and disruption experiments implicated Notch and CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling in hematopoietic progenitor development. Transcriptomic benchmarking revealed HSC-associated molecular features in the generated cells while also identifying residual transcriptional differences from primary cord blood LT-HSCs. The resulting HSPCs exhibited clonogenic activity and multilineage differentiation potential, giving rise to enucleated erythrocytes, cytotoxic natural killer cells, and phenotypically identified monocyte-like and T-lineage cells, with erythroid enucleation reaching approximately 80%. In addition, day-10 suspension-derived CD34+ cells showed detectable bone marrow engraftment in vivo. Collectively, this study shows that key microenvironmental features can be retained within a simplified 2D multicellular system, providing a framework for studying hematopoiesis and refining hPSC-derived HSPC generation. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Recent three-dimensional and organoid-based approaches have highlighted the importance of multicellular microenvironments in hPSC-derived hematopoiesis, but their structural complexity can complicate culture handling and standardization. Here, we established a chemically defined, feeder-free planar system that directed lateral plate mesoderm toward hemogenic endothelium while supporting spontaneous emergence of endothelial, stromal, and hematopoietic populations. The resulting HSPCs exhibited features of definitive hematopoiesis, including clonogenic activity, multilineage differentiation, and evidence of bone marrow engraftment in vivo. Disruption experiments targeting DLL4/Notch and CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling supported a role for this multicellular microenvironment in progenitor output. This work shows that key multicellular microenvironmental features can be retained within a simplified planar culture, providing a framework for studying hematopoiesis and refining hPSC-derived HSPC generation.

records.title: The gastrointestinal KATP-ERK signaling axis: Molecular mechanisms, pharmacological opportunities, and emerging translational technologies.
records.abstract: ATP-sensitive potassium channels are metabolic sensors that couple intracellular nucleotide availability to membrane excitability, calcium signaling, mitochondrial function, and cell survival. Growing evidence identifies KATP channels as essential regulators of gastrointestinal physiology. They are expressed in smooth muscle, enteric neurons, interstitial cells of Cajal, epithelial and enteroendocrine cells, microvascular cells, pericytes, and liver, where they contribute to motility, secretion, barrier integrity, nutrient sensing, vascular regulation, and mucosal protection. In parallel, ERK1/2 are central effectors of the MAPK pathway, controlling epithelial renewal, inflammation, fibrosis, apoptosis, and tissue repair. This review proposes an integrated KATP-ERK signaling network that regulates gastrointestinal homeostasis. PubMed and Scopus were searched for relevant studies using combinations of the terms "ERK" AND "KATP channels" AND "cardiovascular" OR "gastrointestinal". Evidence supports functional crosstalk between KATP channels and ERK signaling. In this framework, KATP channels act as metabolic rheostats, whereas ERK integrates redox, growth factor, and stress-related signals. Acute KATP activation promotes adaptation by preserving mitochondrial function and epithelial barrier integrity, whereas chronic channel overactivation, as observed in Cantú syndrome caused by gain-of-function mutations in ABCC9 or KCNJ8, may induce maladaptive remodeling, tight junction disruption, apoptosis, fibrosis, and dysmotility. The potential involvement of FGFR/Klotho signaling as an upstream ERK regulator, together with KATP/ERK pharmacological modulation, FGF/Klotho-based therapies, and biosensor technologies for pathway monitoring in organoids and gut-on-chip models, is also discussed. The KATP-ERK-FGFR/Klotho framework links ion-channel pharmacology with gastrointestinal biology, providing a foundation for biomarker discovery, therapeutic development, and precision medicine approaches in gastrointestinal disorders.

records.title: Nanotechnology-driven cryopreservation across cells and 3D constructs.
records.abstract: Cryopreservation is essential for cell-based research, regenerative medicine, and emerging therapies; however, conventional strategies remain limited by ice-induced damage, osmotic imbalance, and cryoprotectant (CPA)-associated toxicity. This review discusses the mechanisms of cryoinjury, limitations of conventional CPA-based strategies, and emerging approaches, including combinatorial CPA formulations and ice-modulating agents such as antifreeze proteins and synthetic ice recrystallization inhibitors. Building on these advances, we evaluate nanotechnology-enabled platforms for precise and multifunctional cryoprotection, encompassing nanocarrier-mediated intracellular CPA delivery, nanomaterial-based extracellular ice modulation, and uniform volumetric rewarming. We further discuss the challenges and emerging nanotechnology-enabled strategies for preserving three-dimensional cellular constructs, including spheroids and organoids, where diffusion limitations, spatial heterogeneity, and structural complexity require tailored preservation approaches. Together, these advances establish nanotechnology as an integrated platform for next-generation cryopreservation by enabling coordinated control of CPA delivery, ice behavior, and rewarming in regenerative medicine and cell-based therapeutics.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: HDAC8 Assistant: a QSAR-guided molecular generation platform for de novo design and virtual screening of HDAC8 inhibitors.
records.abstract: Histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) inhibitors are considered promising therapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer and several other diseases. In this study, regression QSAR models for HDAC8 inhibitors were developed using various types of molecular descriptors and machine learning algorithms. The best-performing weighted consensus model achieved an external predictive performance of Q2test = 0.62 for the complete test set and 0.71 for compounds within the applicability domain, covering 77% of the external data. Model reliability was confirmed by five-fold cross-validation and y-randomization tests. The developed QSAR model was integrated into the HDAC8 Assistant web application (https://hdac8-assistant.streamlit.app/), which includes a de novo molecular generation module based on recurrent neural networks (SMILES-RNN) and reinforcement learning (REINVENT 2). For targeted discovery of novel inhibitors, an original reward function was proposed that combines QSAR-predicted activity with applicability domain control for generated compounds. This approach enables simultaneous optimization of predicted inhibitory activity while limiting extrapolation beyond the model applicability domain. HDAC8 Assistant also implements assessment of drug-likeness according to the Muegge criteria, as well as PAINS, toxicophore, and Brenk structural-alert detection. Molecular docking was performed for the most promising compounds generated by HDAC8 Assistant to analyse their interactions with the HDAC8 active site.

records.title: Programming biological behavior with AI-guided de novo protein design.
records.abstract: Driven by advances in artificial intelligence, de novo protein design can now generate diverse molecular functions from the ground up, achieving remarkable success in engineering binders against many macromolecular targets. Here, we provide a perspective on how de novo design can progress beyond bimolecular interactions toward the bottom-up construction of protein reaction networks. We highlight how programmable, modular, and controllable de novo components can drive complex, emergent biological behaviors. Overcoming current challenges-including designable protein dynamics, multi-step functionalities, and non-equilibrium systems-is essential for this transition. With continued foundational method improvements, the field is poised to pioneer precise protein perturbations for systems-level insight and to engineer emergent cellular behaviors like signal amplification, decision-making, and error correction de novo to fundamentally advance synthetic biology, biotechnology, and medicine.

records.title: Multi-Objective Molecular Generation via Actor-Critic Regulated by Adaptive Cooperative Evolution.
records.abstract: Many complex diseases involve intricate and interdependent biological mechanisms, making multi-target drug design therapeutically important. However, existing molecular generation models often struggle to balance conflicting property requirements, maintain structural exploration, and avoid premature convergence during reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose CMIR-RL, a reinforcement learning-based molecular generation model that integrates cooperative crossover-mutation exploration, structure-based intrinsic rewards, and Pareto-based multi-objective optimization. In CMIR-RL, mutation and crossover networks synergistically guide the agent to balance exploration and exploitation, while Pareto-front-guided reward assignment updates the generation policy under multiple property constraints. Experiments on a three-objective polypharmacology task show that CMIR-RL significantly improves desirability from 0.8868 to 0.9542 over the baseline method, while maintaining competitive validity, uniqueness, and diversity. Additional GuacaMol results further indicate competitive generalization across goal-directed molecular generation tasks. These results show that CMIR-RL is an effective reinforcement learning strategy for early-stage multi-objective molecular design.
records.journal: IEEE transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics

records.title: Virus-like particle vaccines: from antigen architecture to antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses.
records.abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs) mimic key structural features of native viruses while lacking a replication-competent viral genome, combining favorable safety with multivalent antigen presentation and strong immunogenicity. Yet, how VLP design influences the quality and persistence of adaptive immunity remains incompletely understood. This review examines relevant literature identified through targeted searches on recent advances in VLP engineering, with emphasis on particle architecture, antigen-display strategies, and structural determinants of immune recognition. We discuss how VLPs facilitate antigen presentation by antigen-presenting cells and shape CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses, immune memory, and T follicular helper cell-B-cell interactions within germinal centers. Emerging approaches linking VLP design with humoral and cellular immunity are also considered. The next generation of VLP vaccines will require a transition from empirical enhancement of immunogenicity toward precision engineering of immune responses. A major challenge is to establish robust and transferable structure-immunity relationships while addressing manufacturing feasibility, quality control, potency assessment, and product comparability. Advances in computational protein design, structural biology, and high-dimensional immune profiling are expected to enable increasingly quantitative and mechanism-based optimization of VLP platforms. However, fully predictive control over human immune responses will remain a complex challenge.

records.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
records.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A cost-ordered cascade concentrates full structure-based evaluation on a small pre-filtered survivor set, achieving a 2.5 × reduction in candidates advanced relative to those generated. An in-loop metabolic gate enforces Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) safety by writing flagged reactive substructures to a per-target learned state, suppressing identified liabilities from all subsequent generation rounds. A persistent campaign memory influences generation trajectories by embedding prior structural success and failure patterns directly into the design context. We validate these architectural invariants across three structurally diverse benchmark targets (EGFR, KRAS G 12 C , and BRD4) through a five-condition component ablation and a controlled memory ablation, and confirm generator agnosticism across four language-model backends via a deterministic recalibration layer that overrides backend self-evaluation bias. Without explicit chemotype instruction, the pipeline computationally converged toward candidates bearing the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold characteristic of the approved inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, from structural feedback alone. Persistent campaign memory showed directional but non-significant trends toward lower inter-round score variance and higher late-stage advance rate ( n ≈ 90 per condition; all p > 0.20 ). The component ablation reveals that optimizing for a single objective collapses performance on others; only full orchestration resolves this tension. Advancement rates above 79% across all backends confirm that the validated properties are generator-agnostic, enforced by architectural invariants rather than model capability. All reported outcomes are properties of the computational generation process; prospective biochemical validation of the advanced candidates remains the primary direction for future work.

records.title: Functional alignment of protein language models via reinforcement learning.
records.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) enable generative design of novel protein sequences but remain fundamentally misaligned with protein engineering goals, as they lack explicit understanding of function and often fail to improve properties beyond those found in nature. We introduce Reinforcement Learning from eXperimental Feedback (RLXF), a general framework that aligns protein language models with experimentally measured functional objectives, drawing inspiration from the methods used to align large language models like ChatGPT. Applied across five diverse protein families, RLXF improves generation of high-functioning variants beyond pre-trained baselines. We demonstrate this with CreiLOV, an oxygen-independent fluorescent protein, where RLXF-aligned models generate sequences with significantly enhanced fluorescence, including the most fluorescent CreiLOV variants reported to date. Our results indicate that RLXF-aligned models effectively integrate the evolutionary knowledge encoded in pre-trained pLMs with experimental observations, improving the success rate of generated sequences and enabling the discovery of synergistic mutation combinations that are difficult to identify through zero-shot or evolutionary approaches. RLXF provides a scalable and accessible approach to steer generative models toward desired biochemical properties, enabling function-driven protein design beyond the limits of natural evolution.

records.title: A novel multiplex digital PCR assay for simultaneous quantification of androgen receptor amplification, mutations, and splice variants in cell-free nucleic acids from metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
records.abstract: Somatic androgen receptor (AR) alterations including gene amplification, point mutations, and the AR-V7 splice variant occur in 50-70% of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and drive resistance to AR-pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). However, current liquid biopsy approaches typically require separate cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and cfRNA workflows to evaluate these distinct alteration classes, increasing sample input requirements, assay complexity, and cost. Because plasma cell-free nucleic acid yield is often limited, an integrated assay capable of interrogating DNA and RNA-derived biomarkers from a single blood draw remain an unmet clinical need. Here we describe the development and proof-of-concept validation of a novel multiplex multimodal digital PCR (dPCR) assay that co-detects AR copy-number amplification, somatic point mutations (T878A), and the AR-V7 splice variant from plasma cell-free nucleic acids (cfNAs) in a single streamlined reaction. The assay employs RNase H-dependent PCR (rhPCR) primers with ultra-short amplicons (≤68 bp) that simultaneously interrogate both cfDNA and cfRNA, enabling multimodal detection without separate DNA and RNA workflows. Using prostate cancer cell lines with defined AR alteration status, the assay detected AR amplification at 2% of tumor DNA, quantified T878A mutations at a mutant allele frequency as low as 0.024%, and AR-V7 splicing variant with a sensitivity of 0.096% tumor cell fraction. In two mCRPC patient plasma samples, the assay tracked dynamic changes of these AR variants during ARPI therapy, revealing distinct patterns of clonal evolution that are consistent with treatment pressure and clinical outcomes. This multimodal dPCR platform provides a cost-effective, highly sensitive liquid biopsy tool for detection of clinically significant AR alterations and represents a foundation for a laboratory-developed test (LDT) to guide personalized therapy in mCRPC.

records.title: Unipoint-anchored cascade amplification strategy integrating FUSE probe-activated CRISPR-Cas12a for dual mode osteopontin detection toward osteosarcoma assessment and therapeutic response evaluation.
records.abstract: Reliable assessment of disease status and therapeutic response in osteosarcoma remains an unmet clinical need. Integrative bioinformatics analysis and protein-level verification in paired clinical specimens prioritized secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1, osteopontin) as a liquid biopsy target associated with osteosarcoma progression and patient survival. On this basis, CRUMP, a CRISPR-Cas12a and FUSE Probe-based dual-mode biosensing platform, was developed for SPP1 quantification. A bifunctional NH2-ZIF-8 probe co-immobilizes the components required for target recognition and Cas12a activation, while MoS2@AuNPs interfaces transduce the resulting signals. Signal amplification is achieved through a unipoint-anchored multisite cascade based on a DNA tetrahedron-HCR architecture, enabling one-to-multiple parallel amplification while balancing stability and sensitivity. A single Cas12a cleavage event simultaneously decreases the electrochemical (EC) signal and increases the fluorescence (FL) signal. These reciprocal changes allow the two readouts to provide an internal consistency check for each measurement. Each channel covers more than five orders of magnitude, with detection limits of 167.7 fg/mL for EC and 331.6 fg/mL for FL. The broad measurement ranges allow most serum samples to be analyzed directly, without the per-sample dilution optimization that ELISA requires, and the complete analysis takes only approximately 85 min. Validation across osteosarcoma cell lines, clinical specimens, and tumor-bearing mouse models provided preliminary evidence for the feasibility of CRUMP in SPP1 quantification and endpoint assessment of chemotherapeutic response. By combining biomarker prioritization, biosensor engineering, and preliminary application testing, this work presents CRUMP as a candidate platform for SPP1-based assessment of osteosarcoma and its therapeutic response.

records.title: Rethinking selection criteria for liver transplantation in hepatocellular carcinoma: from morphology to artificial intelligence.
records.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is a uniquely curative treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), as it removes both the tumor and the underlying cirrhotic liver. However, organ scarcity makes candidate selection a central clinical and ethical issue. Over the past three decades, selection has evolved from simple morphologic thresholds toward increasingly multidimensional models of oncologic risk. This review examines the evolution of selection criteria for LT in HCC, from the Milan criteria and subsequent morphology-based expansions to models incorporating tumor biology, serum biomarkers, treatment response, waiting-list dynamics, and artificial intelligence. The literature discussed includes landmark morphologic criteria, AFP-based models, PIVKA-II and AFP-L3 integration, downstaging strategies, dynamic scores such as TRAIN and NYCA, and machine-learning models including MoRAL-AI, TRIUMPH, and TRAIN-AI. The field is moving from categorical eligibility rules toward individualized, continuous risk estimation. Future selection should not aim merely to expand transplant access, but to identify patients most likely to achieve durable oncologic benefit. Artificial intelligence, radiomics, liquid biopsy, and multi-omic profiling may refine risk prediction, but their clinical adoption will require prospective validation, transparency, calibration, transportability, and integration into allocation systems.

records.title: RAS Mutations as Prognostic Biomarkers in Digestive Cancers: From Binary Classification to Variant-Specific and Context-Dependent Risk Stratification.
records.abstract: In digestive cancers, activating RAS mutations - primarily KRAS, less frequently NRAS - are among the most prevalent oncogenic drivers. Their clinical significance depends strongly on the tumor type, disease stage, treatment context, and specific RAS variant. In colorectal cancer (CRC), RAS alterations are well-established predictors of resistance to anti-EGFR therapy. However, KRAS G12C-mutant tumors represent a distinct subgroup with demonstrated sensitivity to KRAS G12C inhibitors. However, growing evidence supports the negative prognostic impact of RAS mutations on both primary CRC and colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) in both post-resection and adjuvant therapies. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), where KRAS alterations are nearly universal, prognostic evaluation has evolved from a binary mutant versus wild-type classification to a more refined approach based on mutation subtype (e.g., G12D/V vs. G12R) and KRAS mutant dosage, both of which influence clinical outcomes. In biliary tract cancers, KRAS mutations occur in a relevant subset and are consistently associated with poor survival. Liquid biopsy approaches increasingly enable noninvasive detection and longitudinal monitoring. In gastric cancer, RAS alterations are less frequent overall but may identify biologically aggressive subsets and may also be associated with inferior outcomes under HER2-targeted therapy in selected populations. This review synthesizes contemporary data supporting RAS alterations as prognostic biomarkers across digestive cancers, highlights practical considerations for integrating variant-level RAS information into risk stratification and trial designs, and discusses how emerging RAS-directed therapies may reshape the prognostic significance of specific molecular subsets.

records.title: RNF152 promoter methylation and gene expression in oral premalignant lesions and oral squamous cell carcinoma: implications for epigenetic biomarker development.
records.abstract: Aberrant promoter DNA methylation represents an early molecular alteration in oral carcinogenesis and has emerged as a potential source of molecular biomarkers for oral cancer. Although RNF152 has been implicated in cancer-related molecular dysregulation, its promoter methylation and expression status have not previously been specifically investigated in oral premalignant lesions (OPML) or oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). RNF152 promoter methylation and gene expression were evaluated in paired tumor/lesion and matched adjacent normal tissues from 30 patients with OSCC and 30 patients with OPML, together with oral mucosal tissues from 15 healthy controls. Matched saliva and serum samples from the patient cohorts were also analyzed to evaluate RNF152 methylation as a potential liquid biopsy marker. Quantitative methylation-specific PCR (QMSP) and quantitative real-time PCR (QRT-PCR) were performed, and associations with clinicopathological characteristics, diagnostic performance, and the relationship between promoter methylation and gene expression were investigated. RNF152 promoter methylation was detected in 36.7% of OSCC tumors and 70.0% of OPML lesions, whereas no promoter methylation was identified in oral mucosal tissues from healthy controls. Promoter methylation was also detected in matched saliva and serum samples from both patient groups. Reduced RNF152 expression was observed in 33.3% of OSCC and 30.0% of OPML tissues. Methylation-associated RNF152 expression loss was identified in 13.3% of OSCC and 30.0% of OPML patients. Among methylation-positive cases, concomitant RNF152 expression loss was observed in 36.4% of patients with OSCC and 42.9% of patients with OPML. Continuous promoter methylation levels were not significantly correlated with tissue gene expression in either cohort. RNF152 promoter methylation demonstrated good discriminatory performance for distinguishing OPML from healthy controls (AUC = 0.867, p < 0.001), whereas its discriminatory performance for OSCC was statistically significant but more modest (AUC = 0.683, p = 0.047). This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of RNF152 promoter methylation and gene expression in oral premalignant lesions and oral squamous cell carcinoma. RNF152 promoter methylation showed greater diagnostic potential for OPML than for OSCC, whereas its performance in liquid biopsy specimens was limited. The incomplete concordance between promoter methylation and gene expression suggests that promoter methylation may contribute to RNF152 downregulation in a subset of cases but is not the sole determinant of its expression. These findings support further evaluation of RNF152 as a candidate component of multimarker epigenetic panels rather than as a standalone diagnostic biomarker. Validation in larger, independent cohorts is required to determine its clinical utility.

records.title: Aptamer-based technologies for extracellular vesicle analysis and engineering: from isolation to functional applications.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are natural mediators of intercellular communication and hold promise for disease diagnosis and drug delivery, yet their intrinsic heterogeneity complicates isolation, molecular profiling, and targeted delivery. Aptamers, owing to their high affinity, specificity, chemical tunability, and scalable synthesis, offer a flexible molecular toolkit to address these challenges. In this review, we highlight recent progress in integrating aptamers into EV research across three interconnected domains: (1) the selection of aptamers against EV-associated surface markers; (2) the development of aptamer-based methods for EV capture and isolation; (3) the use of aptamer-functionalized EVs for targeted drug delivery and immunomodulation. We also discuss outstanding challenges, particularly the need for selection strategies that better preserve native EV epitope conformations and the rational design of multifunctional aptamer architectures. Looking forward, the convergence of aptamer technology with EV biology is expected to enable aptamer-drug conjugates and minimally invasive, dynamic liquid biopsy approaches for major diseases such as cancer, ultimately advancing early diagnosis and precision medicine.
